claim.title: Coupled p-N Scaling of Bayes Gap
claim.statement: The Bayes Gap RBG(M_hat_theta) for a uniform-attention Transformer decreases as a function of the product pN (pretraining prompt length times number of prompts), specifically following a power-law trend BG(p, N) ≈ a + b(pN)^-beta + c/N, which fits the data significantly better than models depending on N or p alone.
claim.test_plan: Train a small uniform-attention Transformer (or a simplified mean-pooling network as per Definition 2.2) on synthetic regression tasks. Sweep N in {100, 500, 1000, 2000} and p in {5, 10, 15, 20}. Compute the Bayes Gap for each (N, p) pair. Fit three models to the pooled data: (1) Joint: a + b(pN)^-beta + c/N, (2) N-only: a + bN^-beta, (3) p-only: a + cp^-gamma. Compare the R-squared values.
claim.evidence_in_paper: Table 1, Figure 2 (left and middle panels), Section 4 Findings (1)
claim.success_criterion: The R-squared of the joint model (pN) is greater than 0.8 and significantly higher (by at least 0.1) than the R-squared of both the N-only and p-only models.
